title: Adaptive column freezing, fluid resize gestures, and filter affordances for large virtualized tables
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: deliver a cohesive set of UX patterns and interactions for very large virtualized tables that make it easier for users to keep context, manipulate columns, and discover sort & filter controls without regressing performance or accessibility. Scope covers: column freezing (pin left/right), fluid pointer + keyboard resize gestures that respect live virtualization, persistent per-column filter affordances, and per-column density overrides. Does not include server-side filtering backends or query design; those will be separate infra tickets.
rationale: Customers regularly report losing context when scrolling wide tables and repeatedly re-applying filters during exploratory analysis. Our existing virtual table component supports resizing and sorting but lacks frictionless pinning and discoverable filter affordances; several support tickets and NPS feedback reference this. Goal is to reduce user friction and support power-user workflows while keeping the rendering performance profile identical under high row counts.
approach: Design a progressive enhancement layered on top of the current virtual table: 1) Lightweight column pin action (menu + drag handle) that converts a column to a pinned state without re-creating the full DOM; 2) Continuous resize behavior that updates column width in the virtualization layout engine but throttles reflow; 3) Per-column mini-toolbar revealed on hover/focus with sort, filter chip, and column actions; 4) Density badge per-column that can override row density for that column's cells (useful for compact numeric columns). Prototype in Figma and validate with 3 power-user sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Pinning: User can pin up to 3 columns to the left and 1 to the right; pinned columns are visually separated and remain in view when horizontally scrolling.
Resize: Pointer drag resizes column in real-time; keyboard +/- adjusts width in 8px steps; virtualization does not drop frames when row count > 100k in perf harness.
Affordances: Hover/focus reveals a compact per-column toolbar with sort, filter, and column menu; all controls are reachable by keyboard and have ARIA labels.
Density override: Users can set a compact/regular/comfortable density per column; density changes animate height and do not break row alignment.
Accessibility: Screen reader announces pinned state and current column width; filter button exposes popover with accessible form controls.
Telemetry: Events emitted for pin, unpin, resize, density-change, and filter-open; events include column key and user-initiated/keyboard source.
Docs: Console component docs updated with examples, API for pin/resizable options, and migration notes for existing table usage.
Performance: End-to-end benchmark shows <=10% p99 latency regression on tokenized UI with 50k rows compared to baseline virtual table.
design_notes:
- Use subtle sticky shadow separator when pinned columns start.
- Visual affordance: small pin icon appears on column header hover and in header menu.
- Use transform-based sticky positioning (translateX) to avoid layout thrash in large tables.
- Limit max pinned columns to 4 to avoid cramped layouts.
- Density per-column should default to table density but allow override via column menu.
tradeoffs: - Real-time resize + virtualization improves UX but risks more layout churn; mitigated via throttling reflow and transform positioning.\n- Per-column density adds complexity to cell height alignment; we will animate height and then perform a single sync layout pass to align rows.\n- Offering many pin positions increases implementation complexity for the virtualization engine (we opted to support left and right pinned zones only).
decisions: Implement left and right pinned zones only (no arbitrary insert positions)
Expose keyboard resize (+/- and Home/End to min/max) for accessibility
Per-column toolbar will be present on hover and keyboard focus, with explicit open via Enter
Use CSS transforms for pinned column positioning to keep main scrollable layer as the rendering surface
implementation_notes: Engineering should coordinate with runtime team to avoid rehydrating the full DOM on pin/unpin. Suggested API: columns[] with properties { key, pinned: 'left'|'right'|null, minWidth, maxWidth, densityOverride }. Provide helper methods: table.pinColumn(key), table.resizeColumn(key,width).
qa_checklist: Keyboard navigation: Tab/Shift-Tab reaches toolbar; Enter opens filter popover
Screen reader: Pinned state and width announced
Large dataset perf (50k, 100k rows) smoke tests
Cross-browser: Chrome, Safari, Firefox layout parity
ux_research: Planned: 3 moderated sessions with data analysts (45m each) comparing current table vs prototype. Success metrics: time to locate a target column, time to apply a filter, perceived control over layout (Likert).
notes: Slack thread #ds-tables has ongoing feedback; PM requested a fallback when pinned columns exceed viewport width (clip + show overflow indicator). We'll implement an overflow chevron that opens a compact menu.
outstanding_questions: Should pinned columns be preserved per-user as a preference or per-component state? (PM leaning: per-component, but allow opt-in user presets)
How should column density interact with row grouping/expandable rows?
What telemetry thresholds should trigger auto-rollback of real-time resize if it causes frame drops in low-end devices?
